subject: HelioPay acceptance: load test plan and evidence playbook
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Santiago Ruiz <santiago.ruiz@heliopay.com>, ops@heliopay.com
Cc: Alyssa Kim <alyssa.kim@heliopay.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T15:20:00Z
Subject: HelioPay acceptance: load test plan and evidence playbook

Hi Santiago / HelioPay ops team,

Thanks again for the productive demo yesterday. As discussed, we want to lock the acceptance criteria and the run plan so both teams can execute the onboarding load tests next week. High-level items attached: the proposed load profile (heliopay-loadplan-v1.csv) and a short checklist of telemetry we need from your side.

Acceptance targets we propose for the initial gate:
- 99th percentile latency <= 450ms for auth-and-routing flows at nominal traffic (100 req/s)
- Sustained throughput at 250 req/s for 10 minutes with error rate < 0.5%
- No tail latency spikes > 1.2s during the 95th-99th percentile window

Please confirm these targets or provide any constraints from your side (burst windows, peak hour expectations, regional routing).

Planned test window: 2026-10-05 09:00–12:00 PT (open to shifting by +1 day). We'll run a short canary, then ramp to sustained throughput.

Pre-run asks for HelioPay ops:
- Provide a service account with metric export to our evidence bucket (instructions in CSV)
- Confirm API keys and any IP allowlists for Redwood test agents
- Share a brief list of synthetic flows (sample payloads) if you want us to mirror specific production variations

Attachments: heliopay-loadplan-v1.csv

If this looks good I will copy Monica and Ben to coordinate the runbook and telemetry handoff.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Santiago Ruiz <santiago.ruiz@heliopay.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, ops@heliopay.com
Cc: Alyssa Kim <alyssa.kim@heliopay.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: HelioPay acceptance: load test plan and evidence playbook

Diego,

Thanks — confirmed. The targets look reasonable for our current staging cluster. A couple of notes from our side:
- We can provide the service account and metric sink by 2026-10-04 EOD.
- Peak traffic for the auth flow is closer to 180 req/s, so your nominal 100 req/s is conservative; the 250 req/s sustained looks fine for stress testing.
- We will throttle third-party credit checks during the run to avoid external variability.

Can we start the canary at 09:15 PT so our ops team can be on standby? Also please include a short rollback checklist in the runbook (iptables rule and token revoke) — Alyssa is copied.

Regards,
Santiago Ruiz
SRE Lead, HelioPay

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Santiago Ruiz <santiago.ruiz@heliopay.com>, Alyssa Kim <alyssa.kim@heliopay.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: HelioPay acceptance: load test plan and evidence playbook

Team — looping in runbook owners and infra. Quick checklist before the run (I added a template runbook attachment):

Pre-run readiness (action owners):
- Ben: prepare Redwood test agents, confirm client certs and IPs (attachment: runbook-template.pdf)
- Laura: verify metric collector and trace sampling settings; validate export to HelioPay S3/gcs bucket (we need metrics for 7d retention)
- Diego: confirm timing and vendor throttles, and share final synthetic payload list from HelioPay ops

Run sequence (high level):
1) Canary 15m at 30% target -> smoke checks (error rate, request success)
2) Ramp in 3 steps to sustained throughput (100 -> 180 -> 250 req/s) with 5-minute holds
3) 10-minute steady-state run at 250 req/s with full telemetry capture
4) Cooldown and artifact bundle upload + automated evidence collection

Rollback criteria (quick):
- Error rate > 1% for 2 consecutive minutes
- 99th percentile latency > 1.2s for longer than 3 minutes

I will hand the final runbook to Ben by EOD 2026-10-04. HelioPay: please confirm service account and whether you want us to post artifacts to your Drive or use our shared bucket.

Thanks,
Monica
Senior Customer Success Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Santiago Ruiz <santiago.ruiz@heliopay.com>, Alyssa Kim <alyssa.kim@heliopay.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T10:45:00Z
Subject: Re: HelioPay acceptance: load test plan and evidence playbook — results and artifacts

Quick results from the 2026-10-05 run (attached artifacts: load-run-20261005-results.json, latency-heatmap.png):

Summary:
- Canary (09:15–09:30 PT): passed — error rate 0.08%, no client-side failures
- Ramp to 250 req/s: sustained for 10 minutes with average error rate 0.23%
- 99th percentile latency: 420ms during steady-state; brief spike to 980ms during a 90s window when a third-party credit check timed out (we had that throttled as planned)
- No persistent tail > 1.2s; overall meet acceptance with one expected third-party blip

Artifacts uploaded: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1HelioRunArtifacts (includes full metrics CSV, traces, and our annotated runbook)

Next steps:
- HelioPay: confirm whether the brief credit-check spike is acceptable for the gate or if you want an additional run with alternate throttling rules.
- Diego/Monica: if HelioPay signs off, we can mark onboarding acceptance and schedule production rollout checklist.

Thanks everyone — great coordination.

Ben Carter
Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
